title: The Lost Boy
content:
Man, this is one of the albums that had me in a chokehold for a long time. I remember discovering Cordae back in late 2018 when he still repped YBN and I patiently waited for his debut album while listening to some singles and features he had before the album.

Then, the album dropped and 16-year-old me could not stop playing this album. I distinctively remember walking slow to class just to listen to some of the tracks in the album and all I can say is this is Cordae's best work in terms of his whole discography. The Lost Boy represents an album of which Cordae tells his story to the world. 

This album showcased how much raw talent he had in his freshman years and the potential that could be unlocked in his raps. The album is a very respectable project for a debut album. I like the sweet laid-back production throughout the album, mixed alongside with the laid-back flow and bars and this album sounds like you've dug up gold in a mine. The album is layered very well, and I like how he expresses his aspirations, goals, and anxieties in a bold and thoughtful manner. The album was later nominated for Best Rap Album at the 2020 Grammy Awards, while the album track "Bad Idea" was nominated a Grammy Award for Best Rap Song.

**Not giving this album, a 5 Star would be a betrayal to my younger self.** 

*My three Stand-Out tracks within this album have to be:*

*Bad Idea (feat. Chance The Rapper), Wintertime and Been Around.*
verdict: Cordae's best album so far and I would recommend going listen to it if you've haven't done so.
